comment: There's a short reflection on the reading due before every class and three essays throughout the semester. Dr. Fennessey is somewhat a tough grader, but he gives extremely detailed feedback. The course content is interesting, and people do participate in discussion. Overall, it's okay to take for gen ed.

I only took this course because I needed another class and it fulfilled the history requirement. I was not particularly passionate about the subject but Professor Fennessy is and it makes it significantly more engaging. He is a very reasonable grader and easily accessible outside of class. I would not deter someone from taking this course
Dr. Fennessy is great!! Take his class, you won't regret it

Dr. Fennessy was able to make an intro class actually interesting. It wasn't a boring textbook, but readings from books and papers that we talked about and linked together. I liked being able to tie it to modern-day stuff also. He's available outside of class for brain-storming and answering questions. Definitely recommend!

Brian K. Fennessy is a tad self-absorbed dare I say. He gives a ton of work and grades pretty harshly for a gen-ed. He likes to listen to himself talk clearly, but doesn't engage the rest of the class in any meaningful discussionoften leading to the room turning into nap time.

He has high expectations for writing and participation, but he really cares about helping his students improve. I honestly thought history was boring until I took this class. He keeps things interesting by mixing up lecture with discussion and group activities. Readings are pretty reasonable, usually less than 30 pages.

For lectures, he is very well prepared and he knows what he should talk about. As a professor, he is still immature. He assigns a lot of reading to his students, he assigns homework that is meaningless, and the exam format is ridiculous. His grading is bad. So far, he is a scholar who is passionate about his subject, but he is not a good professor

Lots of useless readings and boring lectures. Very tough grader and gives horrible feedback. Doesn't know how to run the class and criticizes everything that his students say. Would not recommend taking one of his classes.

Very boring and tedious. He talks the whole class and it's not very interactive. There is lots of reading for a 100 level class and he just lectures and loves to hear himself talk. He also says he doesn't want you to memorize history but then has a lot of timelines so you dont really learn much. Does not know how to run a class but is passionate

For a history gen ed, this class was the way to go. Although at some points readings were long and not always the most interesting, it was better than some of the other options and I can say that I have definitely learned a lot about music in his class. He is there to help if you need it, and keeps things interesting. Definitely a good gen ed.

Had him for Social History of American Pop Music. Dr. Fennessy is a good prof. Really guides students through the history and what he expects from you. The readings are really not that much, most of the time only up to 30 pages, a few easy homeworks. As long as you give insightful and well thought out comments you should be fine.

Fennessy has a lot of potential as a professor. He is knowledgeable about what he teaches and the information is very interesting, although I wish his teaching style was more interactive because we have small enough classes to do that and also that he could be a bit more positive with students. Some small changes would make a great difference.
Worst prof. Loved to listen to himself talk. Horrible and tedious homework assignments that don't teach you anything. just avoid it at all costs.

This was 100% the worst history class I've ever taken. He assigns hours of reading that don't help you learn, and assignments that waste your time. He can't run a class, he just draws timelines and talks at his students. Also, he is incredibly full of himself and uses class time to compliment his own writing. All of his students are miserable.

If I could give 0 stars I would. He expects students to do A LOT of reading and pointless assignments. He's young and doesn't know how to run a class or teach yet. He's also full of himself. This is one of the worst and most boring classes I've ever taken. If you don't love history or don't want to be a history major do not take this class.
